blocks.text: Use case diagrams are a fundamental part of UML used to show the ways in which users, called actors, interact with a system. They give a visual view of the system's functionality from the user's perspective, helping to identify the requirements and the interactions between users and the system.

blocks.title: Use case
blocks.text: A use case is a description of a set of interactions between a user (actor) and a system to achieve a specific goal. Each use case represents a complete workflow from the user's perspective, detailing the steps involved in accomplishing a particular task.

items: Capturing functional requirements: identifying and documenting what the system must do.
Understanding user interactions: how different users will use the system.
Planning and testing: planning development and designing test cases to check the system's functions.
Identify actors: the types of users, people or other systems, who will interact with the system.
Define goals: what each actor needs to accomplish with the system.
Outline interactions: describe the interactions that achieve these goals; each one with a significant outcome is a possible use case.
Validate use cases: review them with stakeholders to check they capture the required functions and interactions.

blocks.text: In Figure 1.9 a library system's use case diagram shows two actors, a librarian and a student, both connected to the use cases Borrow book and Return book inside the system boundary. In the book's class activity on an online shopping platform, the actors are the customer, the administrator and the delivery personnel, and the use cases are browse products, add items to cart, make purchase, manage product listings, process orders, handle customer inquiries and update delivery status.

blocks.prompt: Which of these is a purpose of use case diagrams (MCQ 10)? Explain the purpose of a use case diagram (short question 6).
blocks.explanation: To identify and document the system's functional requirements, option (b). A use case diagram shows who uses the system (actors) and what each of them achieves with it (use cases), so it captures the required functions, helps plan development and gives the basis for test cases.

blocks.prompt: Long question 4: list the actors and use cases for a use case diagram of an online banking system.
blocks.explanation: Actors: customer, bank staff (and possibly the payment network as an external system). Customer use cases: log in, view balance, view statement, transfer money, pay bills. Staff use cases: open account, verify customer, approve loans, handle complaints. Draw the actors outside a system box and connect each to its use-case ovals inside it.

items: Use case diagram: actors and the use cases (goals) they achieve with the system; captures functional requirements, user interactions, planning and testing.
Steps: identify actors, define goals, outline interactions, validate; Fig. 1.9 library (librarian, student; borrow, return book).
